parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Electromagnetic radiation of a single constant frequency is incident on a metal surface. This causes an electron to be emitted.

Explain why the maximum kinetic energy of the electron is independent of the intensity of the incident radiation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem: Ultraviolet radiation of wavelength $250\text{ nm}$ is incident on the surface of a sheet of zinc. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is $1.4\text{ eV}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: the energy of a photon of the ultraviolet radiation

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the work function energy of the surface of the zinc.
